context: Modules over commutative unital rings; equivalent finiteness axioms / finite-generation
editorial_note: ProofWiki Definition:Noetherian Module gives three equivalent definitions over a commutative ring with identity. The finite-generation, ascending-chain and maximal conditions quantify over submodules, not arbitrary subsets and not ideals of an unrelated ring. When R is an R-module, submodules correspond to ideals, supporting the independently screened Noetherian-ring-as-module formulation after the separately sourced module definition exists. The condition for submodules is not itself a circular definition of a Noetherian module. Source section: Definition 1
text: A module M over a commutative ring A with identity is Noetherian when every A-submodule of M is finitely generated.

context: R-linear subgroup of a module stable under scalar multiplication / subgroup-stable
editorial_note: The ProofWiki source requires a module structure on the subset inherited from M, along with closure under the scalar operation. In standard algebra these requirements are equivalent to being an additive subgroup stable under all scalar multiplication. The definition does not say that any arbitrary subset of M is automatically a submodule and must not be merged with an ideal of a ring, even though ideals are special submodules of R. Source section: Definition
text: For a left R-module M, a subset N⊆M is a submodule when N is an additive subgroup of M and rn∈N for every r∈R and n∈N, with the addition and scalar multiplication restricted from M.

context: Topology P(S) on a nonempty set S (source scope) / powerset
editorial_note: ProofWiki's direct definition explicitly assumes S is nonempty and defines the discrete topology as its entire power set. The same construction also makes sense for the empty set, but that extension has not been separately cited in this batch. The nonempty version is sufficient to define the two-point discrete target in the connectedness characterization. Do not confuse a discrete topological space with a discrete category. Source section: Definition
text: For a nonempty set S, the discrete topology is τ=P(S), the family of every subset of S; thus every subset is open in the resulting topological space (S,τ).

context: Mapping between topological spaces, equivalent global and pointwise forms / inverse-images-of-open-sets
editorial_note: ProofWiki explicitly separates continuity everywhere by preimages of open sets and continuity at each point by open-neighborhood containment. The two formulations are equivalent for arbitrary topological spaces, including the empty-domain case. The pointwise statement quantifies over every x∈X; continuity does not require a bijection, openness of f itself, or metric epsilon-delta arguments. The previously inaccessible guessed URL was incorrect; this checked page is the precise accessible source. Source section: Continuous Everywhere / Definition by Open Sets
text: A map f:X→Y between topological spaces is continuous when, for every open subset V⊆Y, the inverse image f^{-1}(V) is open in X.

text: A map f:X→Y is continuous when for each x∈X and each open neighborhood V of f(x) in Y there exists an open neighborhood U of x in X such that f(U)⊆V.
